guide.summary: A water microbe that sends out a signal and starts to glow when many of its kind are close by.
guide.biology: Some bacteria release signal molecules and switch on shared behaviours, such as glowing, only when enough neighbours are nearby.
guide.rules: Lives in water only. Eats metabolite first, then sugar, using oxygen. Moves 0.25 cells per second and senses food up to 2 cells away. While it has more than 35 energy it releases glow signal at 0.02 per second for 0.20 energy per second, stopping where the local signal reaches 1.0. After sensing signal of 0.30 or more for 5 seconds it glows, costing 0.30 energy per second; it stops after sensing 0.15 or less for 5 seconds or when its energy falls below 15. The glow is only for show and gives no light.
guide.example: Place one Lantern on its own and a crowd of Lanterns elsewhere, and see which ones start to glow.
